title: FMCSA New Motor Carrier Leads: New Authority, Email & Phone

mode.title: Mode
mode.description: newCarriers (default) = the feed of carriers newly added to the FMCSA census in the last N days. lookup = look up specific carriers by USDOT number, MC/MX number or company name, any registration date; the date window, 'Only new since last run' and 'Only carriers with an email' are ignored.
mode.sectionDescription: Pick the daily new-carrier feed, or look up specific carriers. Most runs leave this on the default.

states.title: States (2-letter)
states.description: Two-letter state codes to include, e.g. ["TX","FL","GA"]. Leave empty to get new carriers from every US state.
states.sectionDescription: The few settings most runs need. The prefilled values give a small, fast test run.

daysBack.title: New in the last N days
daysBack.description: Only carriers added to the FMCSA census in the last N days. 7 = this week's new authorities. Use 1-3 for a daily scheduled feed.

maxResults.title: Max results
maxResults.description: Hard cap on carriers returned, and charged, in this run. Each carrier is $0.0035 through October 21, 2026, then $0.008 (1,000 = $8).

requireEmail.title: Only carriers with an email
requireEmail.description: Return only carriers with an email address on their FMCSA filing. In our June 2026 sample of the 200 newest carriers, all 200 had one.

onlyNewSinceLastRun.title: Only new since last run (deduped)
onlyNewSinceLastRun.description: Skip any carrier (by USDOT number) you already received in an earlier run, so you are never charged twice for the same carrier. Turn off to re-pull the same window.
onlyNewSinceLastRun.sectionDescription: Optional. Safe to leave as they are; the defaults suit most runs.

requirePhone.title: Only carriers with a phone
requirePhone.description: Return only carriers with a phone or cell number on file.

carrierOperation.title: Carrier operation type
carrierOperation.description: Interstate = hauls across state lines. Intrastate = operates inside one state only.

minPowerUnits.title: Minimum power units (fleet size)
minPowerUnits.description: Only carriers with at least this many trucks (power units). 0 = no minimum. Most new authorities run 1-5 trucks.

maxPowerUnits.title: Maximum power units (fleet size)
maxPowerUnits.description: Only carriers with at most this many trucks. 0 = no maximum.

minDrivers.title: Minimum drivers
minDrivers.description: Only carriers reporting at least this many drivers. 0 = no minimum.

maxDrivers.title: Maximum drivers
maxDrivers.description: Only carriers reporting at most this many drivers. 0 = no maximum.

hazmatOnly.title: Hazmat carriers only
hazmatOnly.description: Return only carriers flagged as hazardous-materials carriers in the FMCSA census.

forHireOnly.title: For-hire trucking companies only
forHireOnly.description: USDOT numbers are also issued to businesses that only move their own goods (contractors, landscapers, home improvement firms). Turn this on to keep only carriers registered as authorized or exempt for-hire, i.e. companies that haul freight for others. About 3 in 4 new registrations pass (Sept 2026 data).

authorityStatus.title: Operating authority status
authorityStatus.description: Keep only carriers whose operating authority (MC/MX docket) has this status in the FMCSA authority history. Brand-new carriers are usually Pending until their authority is granted. 'Any' (default) applies no filter.

includeAuthority.title: Include operating authority fields
includeAuthority.description: Adds authority_type, authority_status, authority_granted_date and per-docket history from the FMCSA authority dataset (one extra free public API call per 100 carriers). Turn off to skip it.

cargoTypes.title: Cargo types (any of)
cargoTypes.description: Only carriers that declare at least one of these cargo types on their filing. Keys: genfreight, household, metalsheet, motoveh, drivetow, logpole, bldgmat, mobilehome, machlrg, produce, liqgas, intermodal, passengers, oilfield, livestock, grainfeed, coalcoke, meat, garbage, usmail, chem, drybulk, coldfood, beverages, paperprod, utility, farmsupp, construct, waterwell, cargoothr.

nameContains.title: Company name contains
nameContains.description: Only carriers whose legal or DBA name contains this text (case-insensitive), e.g. LOGISTICS.

companyName.title: Company name (lookup mode)
companyName.description: Lookup mode: find carriers whose legal or DBA name contains this text (case-insensitive), e.g. WERNER. Same matching as 'Company name contains'; use either one.

dotNumbers.title: USDOT numbers (lookup mode)
dotNumbers.description: Look up these exact carriers by USDOT number, any registration date. When set, the 'new in the last N days' window is ignored. Turn off 'Only new since last run' and 'Only carriers with an email' to get every listed carrier.

mcNumbers.title: MC numbers (lookup mode)
mcNumbers.description: Look up carriers by MC (operating authority) number, digits only. Same behavior as USDOT lookup; can be combined with it.

socrataAppToken.title: Socrata app token (optional)
socrataAppToken.description: Free app token from data.transportation.gov. Only useful for very large or very frequent pulls, to avoid shared rate limits. Can also be set with the SOCRATA_APP_TOKEN environment variable.

webhookUrl.title: Webhook URL (optional)
webhookUrl.description: Optional. Delivered carriers are POSTed here as JSON batches: { source, count, records: [...] }. Use it to push leads straight into a CRM, or an n8n, Make or Zapier webhook.

webhookBatchSize.title: Webhook batch size
webhookBatchSize.description: How many records per webhook POST.

locations.description: Keep only jobs whose location contains one of these strings (not case-sensitive), e.g. "Detroit", "Michigan", "United States".

employmentTypes.title: Employment types
employmentTypes.description: Keep only jobs of these types: full-time, part-time, contract, intern, temporary. Only ATS vendors that publish an employment type can match (Lever, Ashby, BambooHR, Breezy, Personio, Recruitee, SmartRecruiters and schema.org pages do; Greenhouse usually does not). Jobs with no published type are dropped when this is set. Example: ["full-time","contract"].

postedWithinDays.title: Posted within last N days
postedWithinDays.description: Drop jobs posted longer ago than this. Jobs with no posted date are kept. 0 = no limit.

onlyNewSinceLastRun.title: Only new since last run (deduped)
onlyNewSinceLastRun.description: Deliver only jobs you have not received before (tracked per company between runs). Repeat runs then return only newly posted roles, and already-seen jobs are never charged. Turn off to get the full current list every time.

maxJobsTotal.title: Max jobs per run
maxJobsTotal.description: Hard cap on job rows, and charges, across all companies in this run. At $0.002 per job, 5,000 jobs = $10.

includeDescription.title: Include description text
includeDescription.description: Include the job description as plain text. Turn off for faster runs on SmartRecruiters and Workable (one less request per job). Same price either way.

stateStoreName.title: Dedupe store name
stateStoreName.description: Name of the key-value store that remembers which jobs you already received. Use a different name per feed or customer, or change it to start fresh. Example: "acme-weekly-feed".

monitorMode.title: Monitor mode (only new or changed)
monitorMode.description: Recurring-run mode: return only jobs that are new or whose title, location, department, employment type or URL changed since the last monitor run (use a high enough Max jobs per company so the whole board is covered). The first run is a baseline and returns every matching job. Unchanged jobs are not returned and not charged. Each row gets a changeType of new or changed.

reportRemoved.title: Also report removed (monitor mode)
reportRemoved.description: With monitor mode on, also emit one row with changeType "removed" for jobs that were on a company's career board in an earlier run and are gone now, only for companies whose full job board was read this run. Removed rows are free: they are not charged and never count toward your charge limit or max results. Nothing is reported as removed on the baseline run, when the fetch was incomplete or hit a cap, or when your input filters changed since the baseline (the next run re-learns the baseline instead). Default off.

monitorName.title: Monitor name
monitorName.description: Name of the saved baseline. Use a different name per watch list so schedules do not overwrite each other. Default is 'default'. Example: "eng-hiring".

input.description: Fetch open jobs straight from company career pages and ATS APIs (Greenhouse, Lever, Ashby, Workable, SmartRecruiters, Recruitee, BambooHR, Breezy, Personio, schema.org pages, remote-job feeds). searchTerms.title: Search terms (optional)
searchTerms.description: Find apps by keyword with Apple's search API (for example 'meditation' or 'budget tracker'), searched in the first country. The top results per term are added to the app list.

countries.title: Countries (App Store storefronts)
countries.description: Two-letter country codes such as us, gb, de, fr, jp, br, in. Each country has its own reviews, so every app is fetched once per country. 'uk' is accepted as gb.

maxReviewsPerApp.title: Max reviews per app and country
maxReviewsPerApp.description: Cap on reviews returned per app per country. Apple publishes up to 500 recent reviews per app, country and sort order (10 pages of 50). Set 0 to return only app details.

sortBy.title: Sort order
sortBy.description: Most recent (default, works with Since date and delta mode) or most helpful.

searchResultsPerTerm.title: Apps per search term
searchResultsPerTerm.description: How many top search results to take per search term.
searchResultsPerTerm.sectionDescription: Optional. Safe to leave as they are; the defaults suit most runs.

sinceDate.title: Only reviews since
sinceDate.description: Skip reviews older than this. A date such as 2026-09-01, or a relative period such as '7 days', '2 weeks' or '3 months'. Paging stops at the first older review, so old pages are never fetched.

minRating.title: Minimum star rating
minRating.description: Only return reviews with at least this many stars (1-5). Use with Maximum star rating, for example 1-2 to collect complaints only.

maxRating.title: Maximum star rating
maxRating.description: Only return reviews with at most this many stars (1-5).

includeAppDetails.title: Include app details row
includeAppDetails.description: Add one row per app and country with average rating, rating count, price, genre, developer, current version, release notes, size and more.

deltaMode.title: Delta mode (only new reviews)
deltaMode.description: Remember review IDs between runs and return only reviews not returned before. Ideal for scheduled daily monitoring: you pay only for new reviews.

stateKey.title: Delta state name
stateKey.description: Name of the saved state used by delta mode. Use different names for independent monitors. Leave empty to use the name default.

maxApps.title: Max apps
maxApps.description: Safety cap on the number of apps processed in one run.

title: Website Contact Details Scraper: Emails, Phones & Socials $2/1k
description: Website contact extractor: get emails, phone numbers and social media profiles from any list of business websites. One clean row per site with role/named email tags, E.164 phones, 8 socials and address. $0.002 per website (5 pages per site by default); unreachable sites are free.
seo: Website Email & Phone Extractor: Contact Scraper | $2/1k

startUrls.title: Websites
startUrls.description: Business websites to extract contacts from. Paste URLs or bare domains (acme.com). One row is returned per site; duplicates are merged. Upload a CSV/text file of URLs for bulk runs.
startUrls.sectionDescription: The few settings most runs need. The prefilled values give a small, fast test run.

domains.title: Domains (alternative bulk list)
domains.description: Optional plain list of domains, one per line (e.g. acme.com). Merged with Websites above.

onlyWithContacts.title: Only output sites with contacts
onlyWithContacts.description: Skip rows that have no email, phone or social profile. Sites still count as crawled.

maxPagesPerSite.title: Max pages per site
maxPagesPerSite.description: Homepage plus the best contact, impressum, about, team and privacy pages found by link text and URL (in that priority). All pages of a site are included in the one per-site price.
maxPagesPerSite.sectionDescription: Optional. Safe to leave as they are; the defaults suit most runs.

includeNamedEmails.title: Include named (personal) emails
includeNamedEmails.description: Every email is tagged 'role' (info@, sales@, support@...) or 'named' (jane.doe@...). Turn off to return role addresses only.

sameDomainOnly.title: Crawl same domain only
sameDomainOnly.description: Only follow links on the site's own domain and subdomains. Emails on other domains (e.g. a gmail address shown on the site) are still returned and flagged sameDomain=false.

defaultCountry.title: Default phone country
defaultCountry.description: ISO 2-letter country used to normalize local-format phone numbers to E.164 (+13135550142). Country-code domains (.de, .co.uk...) override it automatically.

maxSites.title: Max sites
maxSites.description: Cap on sites crawled (and charged) this run.

maxConcurrency.title: Sites in parallel
maxConcurrency.description: How many sites to crawl at once. Pages inside one site are fetched one after another to stay polite.

siteTimeoutSecs.title: Site timeout (seconds)
siteTimeoutSecs.description: Total time budget per site; whatever was found so far is returned.

title: Shopify Leads: Store Apps, Products & Contacts | $4/1k
description: Shopify leads with 60+ installed apps and theme detected per store. Store name, myshopify domain, country, currency, product count, price range, vendors, activity, emails, phones and socials. Discover stores by niche keyword. $0.004 per store.
seo: Shopify Leads Scraper: Store Apps, Theme & Emails | $4/1k

domains.title: Store domains or URLs
domains.description: Websites to check, one per row (for example allbirds.com or https://www.brooklinen.com/collections/all). Each is tested for Shopify; Shopify stores get a full profile. Non-Shopify sites return a free row with isShopify=false.
domains.sectionDescription: The few settings most runs need. The prefilled values give a small, fast test run.

keywords.title: Discover stores by niche keyword
keywords.description: Optional. Niche words such as 'coffee roaster', 'candles' or 'dog treats'. Finds *.myshopify.com stores whose store name contains the keyword in the public Common Crawl URL index, then analyzes each one. Leave empty to only analyze the domains above.

maxStores.title: Max stores
maxStores.description: Cap on stores analyzed (and charged) this run, across given domains and discovered stores.

crawls.title: Common Crawl snapshots to search (discovery)
crawls.description: How many of the newest monthly Common Crawl indexes to search per keyword. More snapshots find more stores but take longer.
crawls.sectionDescription: Optional. Safe to leave as they are; the defaults suit most runs.

includeProducts.title: Also output products
includeProducts.description: Add one row per product (title, URL, vendor, type, tags, price range, compare-at price, availability, variants, SKUs, image, dates) from /products.json. Charged per product row.

maxProductsPerStore.title: Max products per store
maxProductsPerStore.description: Cap on product rows per store when 'Also output products' is on. Store summaries always use up to 500 products.

includeNonShopify.title: Return rows for non-Shopify domains
includeNonShopify.description: Keep a free row (isShopify=false) for domains that are not Shopify or are closed, so you can filter a mixed list. Never charged.

title: Local Business Leads: No-Website Finder (OpenStreetMap) $3/1k
description: Local business leads at $0.003 per place, including businesses with no website listed. Name, phone, website, email, address, hours, socials and coordinates from OpenStreetMap open data. 75+ types, no-website, phone and website filters, optional email enrichment.
seo: Businesses Without Websites: Local Leads | $3/1k

categories.title: Business types
categories.description: What to search for, one per row. Plain words like dentist, plumber, restaurant, lawyer, hair salon, gym, car repair, real estate (75+ types and common synonyms), or any raw OpenStreetMap tag such as shop=bakery or craft=*. Unknown words are listed in the run summary and skipped.
categories.sectionDescription: The few settings most runs need. The prefilled values give a small, fast test run.

locations.title: Locations
locations.description: Cities, counties, states, ZIP/postal codes or neighbourhoods, one per row, e.g. Austin, TX or Travis County, Texas or 78701, USA. Each is geocoded with OpenStreetMap Nominatim and searched inside its official boundary.

maxItems.title: Max places
maxItems.description: Maximum number of businesses returned (and charged) for the whole run.

requireWebsite.title: Only places with a website
requireWebsite.description: Skip businesses with no website. Skipped places are not charged.
requireWebsite.sectionDescription: Optional. Safe to leave as they are; the defaults suit most runs.

onlyWithoutWebsite.title: Only places with NO website listed
onlyWithoutWebsite.description: Return only businesses that have no website in OpenStreetMap: prospects for web design, SEO and local-marketing offers. Note: 'no website in OpenStreetMap' usually but not always means the business has no site, so check before pitching. Places that do list a website are skipped and not charged.

requirePhone.title: Only places with a phone number
requirePhone.description: Skip businesses with no phone number. Skipped places are not charged.

requireEmail.title: Only places with an email
requireEmail.description: Skip businesses with no email. Works best together with 'Enrich from website', which looks for the email on the business's own site.

enrichFromWebsite.title: Enrich from website (emails, phones, socials)
enrichFromWebsite.description: For each place with a website, fetch its homepage and contact page and extract the emails, phone numbers and social profile links the business publishes there. Charged as a separate event ($0.002) only when the site loads.

bbox.title: Bounding box (optional)
bbox.description: Search a rectangle instead of (or in addition to) named locations: south,west,north,east in decimal degrees, e.g. 30.25,-97.76,30.29,-97.72.

latitude.title: Center latitude (optional)
latitude.description: Search a circle around a point: latitude in decimal degrees, e.g. 30.2672. Use together with longitude and radius.

longitude.title: Center longitude (optional)
longitude.description: Longitude in decimal degrees for the circle search, e.g. -97.7431.

radiusKm.title: Radius (km)
radiusKm.description: Radius of the circle search in kilometres (1-50). Used only when latitude and longitude are set.

title: Workday Jobs Scraper: Any Career Site, 165+ Companies $1/1k
description: Workday jobs from 165+ verified employers or any myworkdayjobs.com site, verified by 64 passing tests. Keyword, location and posted-date filters, full descriptions, salary ranges, remote/hybrid, and only-new-jobs delta mode. $1 per 1,000 jobs.
seo: Workday Jobs Scraper API: myworkdayjobs.com | $1 per 1k

companies.title: Companies (from the built-in directory)
companies.description: Company names from the bundled, live-verified directory of 165+ large employers on Workday, e.g. NVIDIA, Salesforce, Boeing, Pfizer, Target. Use ALL to scrape every company in the directory. Unknown names are listed in the log.
companies.sectionDescription: The few settings most runs need. The prefilled values give a small, fast test run.

searchText.title: Search keywords
searchText.description: Keywords passed to Workday's own search, e.g. data engineer, nurse, sales. Leave empty to list every open role (newest first).

maxItemsPerCompany.title: Max jobs per company
maxItemsPerCompany.description: Stop after this many saved jobs per career site. Workday itself never pages past 2,000 results per query.

careerSiteUrls.title: Workday career site URLs
careerSiteUrls.description: Any public Workday career site URL, e.g. https://nvidia.wd5.myworkdayjobs.com/NVIDIAExternalCareerSite or a job link from it. Tenant, data center (wdN) and site are parsed automatically. myworkdaysite.com URLs work too.
careerSiteUrls.sectionDescription: Optional. Safe to leave as they are; the defaults suit most runs.

locations.title: Location filter
locations.description: Keep only jobs whose location contains any of these words (case-insensitive), e.g. Texas, London, Remote. Multi-location jobs are checked against every location.

postedWithinDays.title: Posted within (days)
postedWithinDays.description: Keep only jobs posted in the last N days, based on Workday's 'Posted N Days Ago'. 0 or empty means no date filter.

includeDescription.title: Include full job description
includeDescription.description: Fetch each job's detail page: full description text, exact posted date, all locations, country, salary range when stated. Billed as Job with description instead of Job listed.

includeDescriptionHtml.title: Also include description HTML
includeDescriptionHtml.description: When descriptions are on, also return the original description HTML (field descriptionHtml) for re-publishing.

onlyNewJobs.title: Only new jobs (delta mode)
onlyNewJobs.description: Remember job IDs in a named key-value store and return only jobs not seen in earlier runs. Ideal for scheduled runs and job alerts; seen jobs are never charged.

deltaStoreName.title: Delta store name
deltaStoreName.description: Name of the key-value store used by delta mode. Use different names to keep separate watch lists.

maxConcurrency.title: Companies in parallel
maxConcurrency.description: How many career sites to scrape at once. Each site is always fetched one request at a time with a pause, to stay polite.

title: Company News Monitor: Brand & Keyword News Alerts, $2/1k
description: Company news monitoring at $0.002 per article from 75 publisher RSS feeds (Bloomberg, CNBC, FT, TechCrunch, PR Newswire...) plus the GDELT news index when reachable. Track companies, domains or keywords. Deduped, event-tagged, delta mode for schedules.
seo: Company News Monitor API: Brand & Keyword Alerts | $2/1k

companies.title: Companies or domains to watch
companies.description: Company or brand names (Stripe, Rivian Automotive) or website domains (stripe.com). A domain is matched by its brand label (stripe) or the full domain in the headline or feed summary.
companies.sectionDescription: The few settings most runs need. The prefilled values give a small, fast test run.

keywords.title: Keywords or topics to watch
keywords.description: Optional extra watch phrases matched as whole words, e.g. "lithium battery", "data breach", "FDA approval". Each returned article lists which companies or keywords it matched.

timespan.title: Look-back window
timespan.description: Only articles published within this window. For scheduled monitoring, use a window slightly longer than your schedule and turn on delta mode.

maxItems.title: Max articles
maxItems.description: Cap on articles delivered (and charged) this run, newest first.

deltaMode.title: Delta mode: only new articles since the last run
deltaMode.description: Remembers delivered articles (by canonical URL and headline) in a named key-value store in your account, so scheduled runs return and charge only articles you have not received yet. The memory is kept per watch list.
deltaMode.sectionDescription: Optional. Safe to leave as they are; the defaults suit most runs.

stateStoreName.title: Delta state store name
stateStoreName.description: Named key-value store that holds the delta memory. Use different names to keep separate monitors fully independent.

sources.title: Sources
sources.description: GDELT DOC 2.0 (global news index, 65+ languages, updated every 15 min) and publisher RSS/Atom feeds. Empty = both.

useBundledFeeds.title: Include the bundled feed list
useBundledFeeds.description: Adds 75 verified business, finance, tech and press-release feeds (BBC, CNBC, Bloomberg, FT, NYT, TechCrunch, PR Newswire, GlobeNewswire, Business Wire and more).

rssFeeds.title: Your own RSS/Atom feeds
rssFeeds.description: Optional feed URLs to add, e.g. a trade publication, a competitor's newsroom feed or a company blog feed.

mustInclude.title: Must also mention (any)
mustInclude.description: Optional. Keep only articles whose headline or summary also contains at least one of these words, e.g. layoffs, acquisition, lawsuit.

excludeWords.title: Exclude articles mentioning
excludeWords.description: Optional. Drop articles whose headline or summary contains any of these words (e.g. a different company with the same name).

eventFilter.title: Event filter
eventFilter.description: Keep only articles tagged with one of these business events. Empty = all articles.

gdeltTimeBudgetSecs.title: GDELT time budget (seconds)
gdeltTimeBudgetSecs.description: Maximum time spent waiting on GDELT (which enforces one request per 5 seconds and is sometimes slow). RSS results are delivered either way.

sourceLanguage.title: Source language
sourceLanguage.description: Optional. ISO code or name, e.g. en, english, de, spanish. Empty = all languages. Bundled feeds are English.

sourceCountry.title: Source country
sourceCountry.description: Optional. Country of the publisher, as ISO code or name, e.g. US, GB, united kingdom, India. Empty = all.

title: Building Permits Leads: US City Permits and Violations, $1.5/1k
description: Building permits leads from official city open-data portals (Chicago, NYC, LA, SF, Seattle, Austin, Baton Rouge, Montgomery Co. MD, Cincinnati). Type, status, dates, valuation, property address, contractor business if published, source link; code violations too. Delta mode. $0.0015 per record.
seo: Building Permits Leads: US City Permits & Violations

cities.title: Cities
cities.description: Which city portals to query. Permits: CHI, NYC, LAX, SFO, SEA, AUS, BTR, MOCO. Code violations: CHI, CIN. Empty = all nine.
cities.sectionDescription: The few settings most runs need. The prefilled values give a small, fast test run.

recordTypes.title: Record types
recordTypes.description: permit = building permits; violation = code-enforcement / building violations (only CHI and CIN publish these here).

sinceDays.title: Since days
sinceDays.description: Return records whose issue date (filing date for San Francisco, violation date for violations) falls in the last N days (1 to 180).

maxItems.title: Max items
maxItems.description: Cap on records delivered (and charged) this run, split evenly across the selected city sources.

keywords.title: Permit type / work keywords
keywords.description: Keep only records whose type, work class or description contains any of these words (case-insensitive), e.g. roof, solar, demolition, new construction, hvac.
keywords.sectionDescription: Optional. Safe to leave as they are; the defaults suit most runs.

minValuation.title: Minimum valuation (USD)
minValuation.description: Keep only permits with a declared project value at or above this amount. 0 = no filter. Violations have no valuation and are not filtered by it.

onlyNewSinceLastRun.title: Only new since last run (delta)
onlyNewSinceLastRun.description: Skip records already delivered in a previous run (tracked by city, record type and permit ID in a named key-value store). A repeat run on the same input delivers 0 rows and charges 0 record events.

stateStoreName.title: Delta store name
stateStoreName.description: Name of the named key-value store that remembers delivered records. Change it to keep separate feeds or to reset delta.

monitorMode.title: Monitor mode (only new or changed)
monitorMode.description: Recurring-run mode: return only permits that are new or whose status, valuation, issue date or contractor changed since the last monitor run. The first run is a baseline and returns everything in scope. Unchanged records are not returned and not charged. Schedule the actor (Schedules tab) to get a recurring feed. Each row gets a changeType of new or changed.

reportRemoved.title: Also report removed (monitor mode)
reportRemoved.description: With monitor mode on, also emit one row with changeType "removed" for permits/violations returned in an earlier run that the city feed no longer returns inside your sinceDays window, only for city sources read to the end. Removed rows are free: they are not charged and never count toward your charge limit or max results. Nothing is reported as removed on the baseline run, when the fetch was incomplete or hit a cap, or when your input filters changed since the baseline (the next run re-learns the baseline instead). Default off.

monitorName.title: Monitor name
monitorName.description: Name of the saved baseline. Use a different name per watch list so schedules do not overwrite each other. Default is 'default'.

title: Sitemap Link Inventory: All URLs + Broken-Link Check, $1/1k
description: Find every sitemap for a domain (robots.txt, nested indexes, .gz, .txt, common paths) and return all URLs with lastmod, priority, images, hreflang, path groups and duplicates. Optional broken-link, redirect, noindex checks. Partial results never fail the run. $0.001 per sitemap file / link checked.
seo: Sitemap Extractor + Broken Link Checker, gz and nested

startUrls.title: Domains or sitemap URLs
startUrls.description: One per row. A bare domain or site URL (https:// is added if missing) triggers discovery: robots.txt Sitemap lines first, then common paths such as /sitemap.xml. A URL that looks like a sitemap (.xml, .xml.gz, .txt, or 'sitemap' in the path) is fetched directly. Public hosts only; private IPs and localhost are refused.
startUrls.sectionDescription: The few settings most runs need. The prefilled values give a small, fast test run.

maxUrlsPerSite.title: Max URLs per site
maxUrlsPerSite.description: Hard cap on unique URLs returned per site. Reading stops (and the download is aborted) once it is reached, so a 2-million-URL sitemap does not stall the run. The site summary says when the cap truncated results.

checkMode.title: Link check mode
checkMode.description: off: inventory only. sitemapUrls: request the sitemap URLs (HEAD, GET fallback) and flag 404, 5xx, unreachable, redirects and noindex. pageLinks: request the internal links found on the pages listed below (or the home page of each start URL). Each request made is a billable 'link checked' event.

maxSitemapFiles.title: Max sitemap files per site
maxSitemapFiles.description: Cap on sitemap files fetched per site, counting index files. Nested indexes are followed up to 6 levels deep.
maxSitemapFiles.sectionDescription: Optional. Safe to leave as they are; the defaults suit most runs.

includeDuplicates.title: Emit duplicate URL rows
includeDuplicates.description: Duplicates are always counted and listed in the site summary. Turn this on to also emit a row (isDuplicate = true) for every repeat occurrence.

pageUrls.title: Pages to scan (pageLinks mode)
pageUrls.description: Pages whose internal links are checked when Link check mode is 'pageLinks'. Leave empty to use the home page of each start URL. The page fetch itself is not billed; each link checked is.

maxLinksToCheck.title: Max links to check
maxLinksToCheck.description: sitemapUrls mode: per site, an evenly spaced sample across the whole inventory (not just the first rows). pageLinks mode: per page. This is the cost ceiling for check mode.

checkIndexability.title: Read noindex signals
checkIndexability.description: Uses a GET for each checked URL (first 256 KB) to read meta robots, plus the X-Robots-Tag header, so noindex pages in the sitemap are flagged. Turn off for HEAD-only, lighter checks.

checkCanonical.title: Flag canonical mismatches
checkCanonical.description: Compare each checked page's rel=canonical with its sitemap URL (trailing slash ignored). Off by default.

checkConcurrency.title: Check concurrency
checkConcurrency.description: Parallel link checks. Requests to the same host are still spaced by the delay below.

requestDelayMs.title: Delay between requests to one host (ms)
requestDelayMs.description: Minimum gap between requests to the same host. A larger robots.txt Crawl-delay (up to 10 s) overrides this.

requestTimeoutSecs.title: Request timeout (seconds)
requestTimeoutSecs.description: Time to first response headers for each request. Slow servers become 'timeout' rows, never failed runs.

timeBudgetSecs.title: Time budget (seconds)
timeBudgetSecs.description: Soft limit for the whole run. When it passes, the actor stops fetching and returns what it has with status 'partial-time-budget'.

userAgent.title: User-Agent
userAgent.description: Sent on every request and matched against robots.txt (the default token is SitemapLinkInventoryBot).

monitorMode.title: Monitor mode (only new or changed)
monitorMode.description: Recurring-run mode: return only sitemap URLs that are new or whose lastmod changed since the last monitor run; sites without lastmod only report new URLs. Best with Check mode off. The first run is a baseline and returns everything in scope. Unchanged records are not returned and not charged. Schedule the actor (Schedules tab) to get a recurring feed. Each row gets a changeType of new or changed.

reportRemoved.title: Also report removed (monitor mode)
reportRemoved.description: With monitor mode on, also emit one row with changeType "removed" for URLs that were in a site's sitemap in an earlier run and are gone now, only for sites whose sitemaps were read completely this run. Removed rows are free: they are not charged and never count toward your charge limit or max results. Nothing is reported as removed on the baseline run, when the fetch was incomplete or hit a cap, or when your input filters changed since the baseline (the next run re-learns the baseline instead). Default off.

monitorName.title: Monitor name
monitorName.description: Name of the saved baseline. Use a different name per watch list so schedules do not overwrite each other. Default is 'default'.

title: Hacker News, npm & PyPI Developer Signals
description: Track Hacker News mentions, Show HN and Launch HN posts, plus npm and PyPI package versions, repo links and download counts, in one dataset. Keyless public APIs. From $0.001 per item.
seo: Hacker News, npm and PyPI Developer Signals

input.title: Developer Signals

modes.title: Modes to run
modes.description: hnSearch: Hacker News stories (and optionally comments) matching your keywords or domains. showHn: Show HN and/or Launch HN posts. npmPackages: npm metadata and download counts. pypiPackages: PyPI metadata and download counts.
modes.sectionDescription: The few settings most runs need. The prefilled values give a small, fast test run.

hnKeywords.title: Hacker News keywords
hnKeywords.description: One search per row (brand, product, competitor, technology). Used by hnSearch; in showHn mode they filter the launches (leave empty to get all recent launches). Example: ["apify","web scraping"].

npmPackages.title: npm packages
npmPackages.description: Package names, scoped names allowed (@scope/name). Returns latest version, description, license, repository, homepage, keywords plus daily, weekly and monthly downloads. Example: ["crawlee","@apify/tsconfig"].

pypiPackages.title: PyPI packages
pypiPackages.description: Package names. Returns latest version, summary, license, Python requirement, project links plus last day, week and month downloads from pypistats.org when available. Example: ["requests","apify-client"].

sinceDate.title: Since
sinceDate.description: Only Hacker News items created after this. An ISO date (2026-09-01) or a relative span such as 30 days, 12 weeks or 6 months. Empty means no limit. Example: "2026-09-01" or "30 days".

maxItemsPerQuery.title: Max items per query
maxItemsPerQuery.description: Cap on Hacker News rows per keyword, per domain and per launch type. Algolia exposes at most 1,000 hits per query. This is your cost ceiling at $0.001 per row.

hnDomains.title: Hacker News domains
hnDomains.description: Find stories that link to a domain, for example github.com/yourorg or yourproduct.com. One per row, no https://.
hnDomains.sectionDescription: Optional. Safe to leave as they are; the defaults suit most runs.

hnIncludeComments.title: Include comments that mention keywords
hnIncludeComments.description: Adds comment rows (recordType comment) for keyword searches. Each comment row is billed as one Hacker News item.

hnSort.title: Sort order
hnSort.description: date: newest first. relevance: Algolia's relevance ranking.

hnMinPoints.title: Minimum points
hnMinPoints.description: Skip stories with fewer points. 0 keeps everything.

showHnKind.title: Launch type (showHn mode)
showHnKind.description: Which launch posts to return in showHn mode.

timeBudgetSecs.title: Time budget (seconds)
timeBudgetSecs.description: Soft limit. When it passes, the actor stops and returns what it has.

input.description: Track developer-ecosystem signals: Hacker News mentions and Show HN launches, npm and PyPI package metadata and download counts. Input: modes[] (hnSearch, showHn, npmPackages, pypiPackages) plus the matching hnKeywords[], npmPackages[], pypiPackages[]; optional sinceDate, hnMinPoints, maxItemsPerQuery. Output: one row per HN item or package with a recordType. Example input: {"modes":["hnSearch","npmPackages"],"hnKeywords":["apify"],"npmPackages":["crawlee"],"sinceDate":"30 days"}.

title: Sanctions Screening: OFAC SDN, EU, UN & UK Lists, Fuzzy Match
description: Screen names of people, companies and vessels against the official OFAC SDN, OFAC Consolidated, UN, EU and UK sanctions lists. Fuzzy match handles diacritics, transliteration, word order and aliases; optional DOB and country. Screening aid, not legal advice. $0.004 per name.
seo: Sanctions List Screening API: OFAC, EU, UN, UK

input.title: Sanctions Screening

names.title: Names to screen
names.description: One name per row: a person, company or vessel. Plain strings work. To add a date of birth, country or type to a name, use the JSON editor and give objects such as {"name": "Ivan Petrov", "dob": "1975-03-02", "country": "Russia", "type": "person"}. Word order, case, diacritics and punctuation do not matter. Up to 5,000 names per run. Example: ["Acme Plumbing Supplies LLC","Rafael Caro-Quintero"].
names.sectionDescription: The few settings most runs need. The prefilled values give a small, fast test run.

lists.title: Sanctions lists to check
lists.description: Which official lists to download for this run. ofac_sdn = US Treasury Specially Designated Nationals (about 19,000 entries). ofac_consolidated = US non-SDN consolidated lists (SSI, FSE, NS-MBS and others). un = UN Security Council consolidated list. eu = EU consolidated financial sanctions list. uk = UK sanctions list (FCDO / OFSI). Each requested list must load for a name to be reported as clear.

minScore.title: Minimum match score (50-100)
minScore.description: A name is flagged possible_match when its best score reaches this value. 100 means identical after normalisation. 85 to 90 is a sensible start for screening; lower it to catch more spelling variants at the cost of more false positives.

maxMatchesPerName.title: Max matches per name
maxMatchesPerName.description: How many of the best-scoring list entries to return for each flagged name (one per list entry, best alias shown).
maxMatchesPerName.sectionDescription: Optional. Safe to leave as they are; the defaults suit most runs.

entityType.title: Default name type
entityType.description: Restrict matching to people, organisations or vessels for names that do not give their own type. 'any' compares against everything.

includeAliases.title: Match against aliases (a.k.a., f.k.a.)
includeAliases.description: On by default. Aliases catch the many sanctioned parties listed under several spellings. Weak or low-quality aliases are included and marked.

monitorMode.title: Monitor mode (only new or changed)

newerThan.description: Relative ("7 days", "2 months") or a date (2026-01-31). YouTube shows comment age as "3 days ago", so the cut is approximate. With 'Newest first' the scraper stops paging at the first older comment.

keywords.title: Only comments containing
keywords.description: Keep comments that contain any of these words (case-insensitive).

minLikes.title: Minimum likes
minLikes.description: Keep only comments with at least this many likes.

monitorMode.title: Monitor mode: only new comments
monitorMode.description: Remember comment IDs between runs (named key-value store) and output only comments not seen before. Schedule the actor daily to get new comments only; seen comments are free.

monitorStoreName.title: Monitor store name
monitorStoreName.description: Use a different name per project to keep separate memories.

language.title: Interface language
language.description: YouTube interface language (hl), affects '3 days ago' texts. Keep 'en' for parsed dates.

videoConcurrency.title: Videos in parallel
videoConcurrency.description: How many videos are read at the same time.

proxyConfiguration.title: Proxy
proxyConfiguration.description: Not needed normally: requests go direct. Pick a proxy only if your runs get blocked.

autoProxyFallback.title: Switch to residential proxy when blocked
autoProxyFallback.description: If YouTube refuses a request twice, retry it through Apify residential proxy (only when your plan includes it).

title: Amazon Best Sellers Scraper: Ranks, 21 Countries, $1.9/1K
description: Amazon Best Sellers, New Releases, Movers & Shakers, Most Wished For and Gift Ideas ranks in 21 countries: rank, ASIN, title, price, rating, reviews, images, category path. Subcategory crawl, rank-change monitor, optional product details.
seo: Amazon Best Sellers Scraper - Top 100 Ranks, 21 Countries

input.title: Amazon Best Sellers Scraper
input.description: Pick a country, list type(s) and categories (or paste list URLs). Output: one row per ranked product with rank, ASIN, title, price, rating, reviews, images and category path. Empty input = top 100 US Best Sellers in Electronics.

categories.title: Categories
categories.description: Department names or slugs as Amazon shows them in the country you pick, e.g. "electronics", "Toys & Games", "kitchen", "Küche, Haushalt & Wohnen". Each is matched against the country's department list; an unknown name lists the valid ones in the log. Leave empty and add no URLs for Electronics.
categories.sectionDescription: Categories by name, or any Amazon list URL (any of the 5 list types, any subcategory). Mix freely.

startUrls.title: List URLs
startUrls.description: Any Amazon Best Sellers / New Releases / Movers & Shakers / Most Wished For / Gift Ideas URL, including subcategories, e.g. https://www.amazon.com/Best-Sellers-Electronics-Camera-Photo-Products/zgbs/electronics/502394/ or https://www.amazon.de/gp/new-releases/kitchen/. The country and list type are read from the URL. A root URL such as https://www.amazon.com/gp/bestsellers/ expands into every department.

listTypes.title: List types
listTypes.description: Which Amazon lists to read for each category above (URLs carry their own type). Movers & Shakers, Most Wished For and Gift Ideas are often empty on Amazon; an empty list is reported in the log and costs nothing.

countryCode.title: Country
countryCode.description: Amazon site for the categories above. Prices are requested in the site's own currency.

language.title: Language
enumTitles: English where Amazon offers it (DE, FR, IT, ES, NL, BE, SE, JP, SA, EG)
language.description: Language of titles and category names. English uses Amazon's own /-/en/ pages; sites without an English version stay in their language.

maxItemsPerCategory.title: Ranks per list
maxItemsPerCategory.description: Top N ranks per list (Amazon publishes 100: ranks 1-50 on page 1 and 51-100 on page 2). 30 or less needs one request per list.

maxItems.title: Max rows (whole run)
maxItems.description: Hard stop for the whole run. You pay per row delivered, so this is also your cost cap.

depth.title: Subcategory depth
depth.description: 0 = only the categories you gave. 1 = also every direct subcategory (e.g. Electronics -> Headphones, Cell Phones, ...). 2 = their subcategories too, and so on.

maxCategories.title: Max lists
maxCategories.description: Upper bound on lists read in one run (each category x list type x subcategory is one list). Protects deep crawls from running away.

minRating.title: Min stars
minRating.sectionDescription: Rows that fail a filter are dropped and not charged.
minRating.description: Keep only products rated at least this many stars, e.g. 4.5.

maxPrice.title: Max price
maxPrice.description: Keep only products at or below this price (site currency). Rows without a price are dropped when this is set.

minReviews.title: Min reviews
minReviews.description: Keep only products with at least this many ratings.

scrapeProductDetails.title: Add product details
scrapeProductDetails.description: Also open each product page: brand, feature bullets, availability, seller, all images, breadcrumbs, best-sellers ranks, bought-in-past-month, model, dimensions, weight, description. One extra request per row; same price per row.

monitorMode.title: Monitor mode (only changes)
monitorMode.description: Remember each list's ranks between runs and output only products that are new to the list or moved rank (with rankLastRun and rankChange). Unchanged products are not output and not charged. Schedule it daily for a cheap rank tracker. The first run outputs everything.

monitorStoreName.title: Monitor store name
monitorStoreName.description: Named key-value store that holds the last ranks. Use a different name per tracker.

proxyConfiguration.title: Proxy
proxyConfiguration.description: Apify datacenter proxy by default (fast and cheap). Each blocked page is retried on a new IP.

autoProxyFallback.title: Switch to residential proxy if blocked
autoProxyFallback.description: If a country keeps blocking the proxy above, switch that country to Apify residential proxy for the rest of the run.

title: SAM.gov Contract Opportunities: Federal Bids & RFPs
description: Get open federal contracts and government bids from SAM.gov: solicitations, RFPs, RFQs, sources sought and award notices with contracting officer email and phone, NAICS, PSC, set-aside, deadlines, full text and attachments. No API key needed; daily new-only monitor mode.
seo: SAM.gov Scraper: Federal Contract Opportunities API

keywords.title: Keywords
keywords.description: Words to search in SAM.gov notices, one search per line (results are merged and de-duplicated). Example: "cybersecurity", "janitorial", "\"cloud migration\"" (quotes for an exact phrase). Leave empty to return every notice that matches the other filters.
keywords.sectionDescription: Combine keywords with codes. Every filter is optional; the prefilled run returns 20 recent software notices in under a minute.

keywordScope.title: Match keywords in
keywordScope.description: "Anywhere" uses SAM.gov's own search box behaviour: it matches the title, description and attached documents, so a parts order with a standard cybersecurity clause can match "cybersecurity". "Title only" returns only notices whose title contains every word of the keyword (fewer, more precise results).
enumTitles: Anywhere (title, text and attachments, like the SAM.gov search box)

naicsCodes.title: NAICS codes
naicsCodes.description: Industry codes, 2 to 6 digits. A shorter code matches every code under it. Examples: 541512 (computer systems design), 541330 (engineering), 236220 (commercial building construction), 561720 (janitorial).

pscCodes.title: PSC codes (product/service codes)
pscCodes.description: Federal product and service codes, upper case. A prefix matches every code under it. Examples: DA01 (IT application development), R4 (professional support services), Z1 (maintenance of real property).

setAside.title: Set-aside types
setAside.description: Only notices reserved for these small-business programs. Leave empty for all, including unrestricted.

enumTitles: Veteran-Owned Small Business sole source, VA (VSS)

noticeTypes.title: Notice types
noticeTypes.description: Which kinds of notices to return. Leave empty for all types. For open bids pick Solicitation and Combined synopsis/solicitation; for early market research pick Sources sought and Presolicitation.

agency.title: Agency or office contains
agency.description: Keep only notices whose department, sub-tier agency or office name or code contains this text (case-insensitive). Separate several with commas. Examples: "veterans affairs", "army corps of engineers", "FA8726".

placeOfPerformanceState.title: Place of performance state
placeOfPerformanceState.description: Two-letter US state codes where the work is performed, for example VA, TX, MI.

postedWithinDays.title: Posted within the last N days
postedWithinDays.description: Only notices posted in the last N days (US Eastern dates). Ignored when Posted from is set. Use 0 for no posted-date limit.

postedFrom.title: Posted from
postedFrom.description: Earliest posted date, YYYY-MM-DD. Overrides Posted within the last N days.

postedTo.title: Posted to
postedTo.description: Latest posted date, YYYY-MM-DD. Defaults to today.

responseDeadlineFrom.title: Response deadline from
responseDeadlineFrom.description: Only notices whose response deadline is on or after this date, YYYY-MM-DD. Useful to skip bids that close too soon.

responseDeadlineTo.title: Response deadline to
responseDeadlineTo.description: Only notices whose response deadline is on or before this date, YYYY-MM-DD.

activeOnly.title: Active notices only
activeOnly.description: Return only notices that SAM.gov lists as active (not archived). Turn off to include archived notices.

includeDescription.title: Include full description
includeDescription.description: Add the full notice text as plain text (HTML removed).

includeContacts.title: Include contracting contacts
includeContacts.description: Add the points of contact published on the notice (usually the contracting officer and specialist): name, title, email, phone.

includeAttachments.title: Include attachment list
includeAttachments.description: Add each attachment's file name, size and download URL (the files themselves are not downloaded). Costs one extra request per notice, so runs take longer.

maxResults.title: Max opportunities
maxResults.description: Stop after this many opportunities are delivered (and charged). SAM.gov serves at most 10,000 records per search.

onlyNewSinceLastRun.title: Only new since last run (monitor mode)
onlyNewSinceLastRun.description: Remember every notice delivered (in a named key-value store) and skip it on later runs. Skipped notices are never charged. Ideal for a daily schedule.

stateStoreName.title: Monitor store name
stateStoreName.description: Name of the key-value store that remembers delivered notices. Use one name per saved search, for example "va-it-bids".

redeliverUpdated.title: Re-deliver amended notices
redeliverUpdated.description: In monitor mode, deliver a notice again when SAM.gov shows a newer modified date (an amendment changes the record). Each re-delivery is charged as an opportunity.

samApiKey.title: SAM.gov API key (optional)
samApiKey.description: Optional. Your own key for the official Get Opportunities Public API (api.sam.gov). Leave empty to use the keyless public source. Note: the official API matches keywords on titles only and has daily request limits per key.
